events.title: Java 8 released
events.summary: Oracle shipped Java 8 on March 18, 2014 with lambda expressions, the Stream API, and java.time — the most widely adopted Java release for a decade.
events.about: Java 8 let developers write `list.stream().filter(...).map(...)` instead of verbose loops, and replaced the broken `java.util.Date` with a modern date/time API. It became the default enterprise Java version and delayed migrations until Java 17/21 LTS releases.

narrative.whyChosen: Java 8 was the functional-programming turning point for mainstream Java.
narrative.whyImportant: Lambdas and streams changed how millions of developers wrote collection and async code.
narrative.problemSolved: Java lacked concise callbacks and modern date handling while competing with C# and Scala.
